title: Prove exact all-depth binomial suffix norms (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped all-depth proof with exact finite corroboration. For the retained triangular Toeplitz parity compiler on `f(z)=1+c z`, the exact maximum forward-suffix infinity norm, over all completed-shear cuts and legal child interleavings, is

```text
N = 2^h
M_h(c) = |c| + M_(h-1)(-c^2),   M_0(c)=1
M_h(c) = 1 + sum_{j=0}^{h-1}|c|^(2^j)
```

At `|c|=1`, suffixes therefore grow exactly as `1+log_2 N` while the completed operator has norm 2. Brian's cited forward-prefix theorem also bounds prefixes by 2. A proper nontrivial cut attains the formula for `c!=0, h>=2`. This adds the exact binomial law and critical-tail suffix obstruction beyond #4731's four-wire witness and common four-cut envelope. No new kappa or supplier admission is claimed.

The result was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Vlado Vojdanovski's retained parity compiler, Cinna Davis's later Gaussian caller, Brian's #4731/#4737 macro-cut results, James Reed's one-level accounting and finite-prefix examples, and their retained predecessor lineage. No predecessor executable is imported or audited.

## Evidence

Before: a general `1/(1-eta)` envelope for eta<1 and a four-wire binomial suffix example. After: the exact all-depth formula, an explicit attaining row and the unit-tail logarithmic separation.

The self-contained standard-library matrix checker passes 48 rational fixtures through N=32, enumerating 223 cut pairs and eight semantic/domain controls. Every constructed pair satisfies `QP=T`; the maximum and attaining row match the formula. For c=1/2, N=8/16/32 give `29/16`, `465/256`, `119041/65536`. For c=1, they give 4, 5, 6.

Both registered warning-strict normal and optimized commands pass. Each direct run took about 0.39 seconds locally; registered replay took about 1.12 seconds, well below the command timeouts. These are verification durations. Generated stdout receipts bind all five package files by SHA256; normal and optimized receipts agree. Package metadata/source validation, committed-byte/source-history preflight and whitespace checks pass on CPython 3.12.15.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/triangular-parity-binomial-suffix
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/triangular-parity-binomial-suffix/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -O -W error -B research/triangular-parity-binomial-suffix/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/triangular-parity-binomial-suffix --check-source-history
```

Expected direct marker: `PASS_BINOMIAL_SUFFIX fixtures=48 controls=8`. Any CPython 3.12 executable can replace the local interpreter path.

## Limitations

The all-complex, all-depth statement rests on the written induction; finite rational fixtures corroborate it. This concerns only binomial symbols and cuts between completed shears. Internal FFT gates, rounded arithmetic, Gaussian gauge conversion, fixed-tape costs, native admission, formal proof-kernel checking and the full selected replay are unrun obligations. No optimum over general symbols with a given tail budget is asserted. The retained eta<1 stability assumptions and selected frontier are unchanged. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

What is the sharp forward-suffix envelope over all unit symbols with tail l1 at most eta<1? Start with exact four-wire even/odd coefficient optimization and a correlation-preserving row invariant. The identity even child is essential to this proof, so the general case remains open.
